'''Nakatomi no Ōshima''' (中臣 大島) was a {{ill|Nobility|en|Nobility|qid=Q134737|lt=noble}} and {{ill|Shi (poetry)|en|Shi (poetry)|qid=Q1759242|lt=Chinese poet}} active during the {{ill|Asuka period|en|Asuka period|qid=Q210688|lt=Asuka period}}. Initially bearing the {{ill|Muraji|en|Muraji|qid=Q2735611|lt=Muraji}} Rank in the {{ill|Nakatomi clan|ar|ناكاتومي|de|Nakatomi (Klan)|el|Αδελφότητα Νακατόμι|es|Clan Nakatomi|fa|خاندان ناکاتومی|fr|Clan Nakatomi|it|Clan Nakatomi|ja|中臣氏|ko|나카토미씨|nl|Nakatomi-clan|pl|Nakatomi (ród)|pt|Clã Nakatomi|vi|Gia tộc Nakatomi|zh|中臣氏|qid=Q1198447|lt=Nakatomi clan}}, he later adopted the titles Nakatomi no Ason, Fujiwara no Ason, and returned to Nakatomi no Ason. He was the son of Nakatomi no Komi and the nephew of {{ill|Nakatomi no Kane|ja|中臣金|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakatomi no Kane|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11366917}}. His court Rank was Chokutai-ni, and he held the position of {{ill|Minister of Divinities|ja|神祇伯|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jingihaku|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q17210025}}.

== Career ==

Following the legacy of {{ill|Fujiwara no Kamatari|az|Fucivara no Kamatari|be|Фудзівара-но Каматары|ca|Nakatomi no Kamatari|de|Fujiwara no Kamatari|es|Fujiwara no Kamatari|fa|فوجیوارا نو کاماتاری|fi|Fujiwara no Kamatari|fr|Fujiwara no Kamatari|hr|Fujiwara no Kamatari|hy|Ֆուձիվարա նո Կամատարի|id|Fujiwara no Kamatari|it|Fujiwara no Kamatari|ja|藤原鎌足|ko|나카토미노 카마타리|nl|Fujiwara no Kamatari|pl|Kamatari Fujiwara|pt|Fujiwara no Kamatari|ru|Фудзивара-но Каматари|sh|Fujiwara no Kamatari|sv|Fujiwara no Kamatari|sw|Fujiwara no Kamatari|th|ฟูจิวาระ โนะ คามาตาริ|tr|Fujiwara no Kamatari|uk|Накатомі но Каматарі|vi|Fujiwara no Kamatari|zh|藤原鎌足|zh_min_nan|Huziwara no Kamatari|qid=Q433995|lt=Nakatomi no Kamatari}} and Nakatomi no Kane, Ōshima served as the head of the {{ill|Nakatomi clan|ar|ناكاتومي|de|Nakatomi (Klan)|el|Αδελφότητα Νακατόμι|es|Clan Nakatomi|fa|خاندان ناکاتومی|fr|Clan Nakatomi|it|Clan Nakatomi|ja|中臣氏|ko|나카토미씨|nl|Nakatomi-clan|pl|Nakatomi (ród)|pt|Clã Nakatomi|vi|Gia tộc Nakatomi|zh|中臣氏|qid=Q1198447|lt=Nakatomi clan}} and became a central figure in both domestic and diplomatic affairs during the reigns of Emperor Tenmu and Empress Jitō. His role in state rituals and governance was significant during the formative period of the {{ill|Traditional Chinese law|en|Traditional Chinese law|qid=Q4380197|lt=Ritsuryō}} system.<ref name="anr">Morikimi Kōshō, "Nakatomi no Ōshima," in the {{ill|Asahi Nihon Rekishi Jinbutsu Jiten|ja|朝日日本歴史人物事典}}</ref>

In 681 CE (10th year of Emperor Tenmu's reign), he was appointed alongside {{ill|Prince Kawashima|ja|川島皇子}}, {{ill|Prince Osakabe|es|Príncipe Osakabe|fa|شاهزاده اوساکابه|fr|Prince Osakabe|ja|忍壁皇子|pt|Osakabe no Miko|qid=Q3403344|lt=Prince Takechi}}, and others to compile and verify historical texts such as the {{ill|Teiki|es|Teiki|fr|Teiki|it|Teiki|ja|帝紀|zh|帝紀 (日本皇室家譜)|qid=Q1107261|lt=Teiki}} and the {{ill|Honji|ja|本辞}}. Ōshima, along with {{ill|Heguri no Koobito|ja|平群子首}}, took an active role in writing these records. At the time, he held the Rank of Daisanjo (大山上).<ref>『日本書紀』Emperor Tenmu10th year 3月17日条</ref> Later that year, he was promoted to Shōkonge (小錦下).

In 683 CE, Ōshima participated in a mission to delineate provincial borders with officials like {{ill|Prince Ise|ja|伊勢王}} and {{ill|Hata no Yakuni|ja|羽田矢国|qid=Q11610319}}, although the task was incomplete.<ref>『日本書紀』Emperor Tenmu12nd year 12月13日条</ref> Following the enactment of the {{ill|Eight Ranks of Nobility|ja|八色の姓|1=Eight Kabane system|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Ranks of Nobility|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Kabane system}} in 684 CE, he changed his Rank from Muraji to Ason and later to Fujiwara no Ason. However, he eventually reverted to Nakatomi no Ason.

In 686 CE, he was dispatched to {{ill|Tsukushi|en|Tsukushi|qid=Q422471|lt=Chikushi}} alongside {{ill|Kawachi-no-Mikoto|ja|河内王|qid=Q17209039}}, {{ill|Otomo no Otomaro|ja|大伴安麻呂|qid=Q11432337}}, {{ill|Sakaibe no Kajiura|ja|境部鯯魚}}, and {{ill|Hozumi Mushimaro|ja|穂積虫麻呂|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hozumi no Muchimaro|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q22129398}} to receive {{ill|Silla envoy|ja|新羅使|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Silla envoys|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q55534500}}.<ref>『日本書紀』朱鳥元年正月条</ref> In 690 CE, during Empress Jitō's enthronement ceremony, Ōshima served as {{ill|Minister of Divinities|ja|神祇伯|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jingihaku|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q17210025}}, delivering a ceremonial address.<ref>『日本書紀』持統天皇4th year 正月1日条</ref>

He passed away on the 11th day of the 3rd lunar month of 693 CE.

== Legacy ==

As a {{ill|Shi (poetry)|en|Shi (poetry)|qid=Q1759242|lt=Chinese poet}}, two of his works are included in the {{ill|Kaifūsō|en|Kaifūsō|qid=Q2334083|lt=Kaifūsō}} anthology. He also contributed to Buddhism, such as initiating the construction of the {{ill|Ōbara-dera|ja|粟原寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Awabaraji Temple|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 粟原寺跡|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11604562}} for {{ill|Prince Kusakabe|en|Prince Kusakabe|qid=Q1046438|lt=Prince Kusakabe}}.<ref>Inscription on the bronze lotus pedestal of Awabaraji's three-story pagoda.</ref>

== Wife: Hime no Ason Nukada ==

The inscription on the {{ill|Tanzan Shrine|ja|談山神社#国宝|lt=bronze lotus pedestal of Awabaraji's pagoda}} indicates that Ōshima's wife, Hime no Ason Nukada, lived nearly 80 years. Scholars like {{ill|Itsuko Okabe|ja|岡部伊都子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okabe Itsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11473814}} and {{ill|Takeshi Umehara|en|Takeshi Umehara|qid=Q3818175|lt=Umehara Takeshi}} have theorized that she may be identical to {{ill|Princess Nukata|en|Princess Nukata|qid=Q119461|lt=Princess Nukada}}, though this remains debated.

== Career Timeline ==

* 681 CE: Appointed Daisanjo; promoted to Shōkonge.
* 684 CE: Name changed from Muraji to Ason under the Eight Ranks of Nobility.
* 686 CE: Participated in Silla envoy reception as Chokutai-shi.
* 690 CE: Served as {{ill|Minister of Divinities|ja|神祇伯|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jingihaku|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q17210025}} during Empress Jitō's enthronement.
* 693 CE: Passed away as Chokutai-ni.
